speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, the Muslim community has shown great concern over the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: But there are also many non-Muslim Singaporeans who are also moved when they see and read about the suffering of the people in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In particular, when we see young innocent children living in poor conditions, being injured or even losing their lives, it tugs at the heartstrings of all of us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Vikram Nair, Ms Usha Chandradas, Assoc Prof Razwana Begum and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked what Singaporeans can do to help those affected in the ongoing conflict and how Singaporeans can express their views while preserving social cohesion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are channels for these views to be shared and heard.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: My colleagues and I have been engaging different groups in many dialogues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are also channels for Singaporeans to provide humanitarian assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Government has supported several public fundraising events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many Members of this House – including the Opposition – have done the same.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: If Singaporeans have other constructive ideas on how we can help those affected, the Government will support them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, I urge all Singaporeans to be cautious about what you see and hear online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain asked about the national security outlook, in light of the increased risk of foreign influence and global uncertainty.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are actors on different sides manipulating social media posts to win people over to their own position.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Such activities are dangerous and I urge everyone to be discerning in looking at the facts and try to understand the complex backdrop against which the current crisis is taking place.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It is challenging – as the conflict has deep roots with a long history spanning decades or centuries, depending on when you consider the starting point to be.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: But it is important as it affects how we respond, both to the situation and to others who might hold different views.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We must not let external events divide us or damage our harmony.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I will now move on to how the Home Team ensures safety and security in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: A key component of our strategy is to minimise re-offending.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Singapore Prison Service (Prisons) and Yellow Ribbon Singapore (YRSG) have been driving efforts to achieve this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They have equipped inmates with skills to get better jobs and helped them manage the challenges of re-entering the workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Prisons has also mobilised community partners to help ex-offenders reintegrate into the society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This is in line with one of the themes in the Forward SG exercise – on doing more to empower those in need, to uplift themselves and their family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Zhulkarnain asked about support for ex-offenders and desistors – those who have stayed clear of crime and drugs after release.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana asked about strategies to incorporate desistance theory into rehabilitation and reintegration programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Prisons recognises that desistance requires an ecosystem of community support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Over 70 agencies are onboard and Prisons is developing a guide of best practices to help desistors form pro-social support groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana also asked about strategies to integrate trauma-informed care into rehabilitation programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Prisons recently incorporated trauma-informed practices in their psychology-based correctional programmes for female inmates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Female inmates who may have experienced trauma, will be equipped to regulate their emotions better to cope with the trauma.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Corrections 2030 is anchored on three key strategies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The first is to strengthen the families of inmates, to reduce intergenerational offending.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana asked about the use of restorative justice in rehabilitation programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Prisons applies restorative practices to help inmates understand the impact of their actions and how they can make amends.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This has been one of Prisons' strategies to curb violence amongst inmates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Prisons will expand the use of restorative practices to help inmates reflect on their role in their family and rebuild their relationship with their family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since 2020, Prisons has been working with MSF and Family Service Centres to support inmates' families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Prisons has also started referring families to self-help groups and other community partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The second strategy is to maximise the employability and career opportunities of ex-offenders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Gainful employment raises self-esteem and provides financial stability – thus reducing re-offending risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under the TAP & Grow initiative, YRSG set up academies in prison to equip inmates with in-demand industry skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To date, YRSG has worked with partners across the precision engineering, media, logistics and food services sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To complement TAP & Grow, YRSG introduced the YR Sandbox to explore opportunities for ex-offenders in emerging and fast-growing sectors, such as the environmental sector, with opportunities for training in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I am pleased to share that in 2024, YRSG will expand YR Sandbox to the hospitality and tourism sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Even as YRSG continues to champion inclusive hiring, it has moved beyond merely securing jobs for ex-offenders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under "Project Beyond Hiring", YRSG equips workplace supervisors with skills to support and empower ex-offenders under their employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This year, YRSG will expand this to more employers across industries, such as logistics and hospitality.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The third strategy is to mobilise community partners to better support rehabilitation and reintegration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This improved long-term desistance is likely due to the strong pro-social support ex-offenders receive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Efforts by volunteers and partners in the community complement Prisons' rehabilitation efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Under this framework, Prisons will equip volunteers with specific competencies needed for their work, such as grief and trauma management.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This year marks the Yellow Ribbon Project's 20th anniversary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To commemorate this, we want to encourage community partners and ex-offenders to advocate for second chances more actively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For instance, ex-offenders will be involved in "Moving HeARTs in the city" – an art exhibition in a roving truck and will conduct workshops and perform music to raise awareness of the Yellow Ribbon Project.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked for a review of the Registration of Criminals Act to further support ex-offenders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MHA periodically reviews the spent regime for criminal records.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In our last review in 2021, we found the current regime appropriate for facilitating the reintegration of ex-offenders – in particular, those who committed minor crimes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Besides the spent regime, there are other initiatives that support reintegration, including those under Corrections 2030, which I shared earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It embodies the spirit of Forward SG – where we seek to temper unequal outcomes, uplift those in need and prevent them from being trapped in a vicious cycle.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The MMOs Rehabilitation Network was established to help MMOs to enhance their collaboration and leverage on each other’s expertise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It has made good progress in supporting rehabilitation efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Malay Activity Executive Committees Council under the People's Association, or MESRA, introduced courses such as financial literacy to residents of the Pertapis Halfway house, Jamiyah and Rise Above to help them better manage their lives as they re-integrate into society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: More than 150 residents have benefited from it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some MMOs have set up a referral system among themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, FITRAH refers cases requiring education assistance to MENDAKI.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This effort has helped beneficiaries who may not know where to seek help for certain issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Last month, MHA organised the inaugural MMO Rehabilitation Network Conference to promote greater collaboration between MMOs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Syed Harun Alhabsyi spoke about the importance of community partnerships in preventing drug abuse.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We agree and will continue to work with the community in Preventive Drug Education (PDE).

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To date, CNB has been working with many MMOs to organise more than 140 events under Dadah Itu Haram campaign, to encourage the Malay/Muslim community to lead drug-free lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: CNB will equip mosques with resources to organise their own drug-free initiatives and further expand the PDE. : Sir, the Minister spoke earlier about how we are addressing the youth drug problem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I will speak on firstly, how we are improving support for drug abusers undergoing rehabilitation; and secondly, enforcement against drug activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza, Mr Keith Chua and Mr Syed Harun Alhabsyi asked about efforts at treating drug abusers and preventing recidivism, including through community intervention.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Prisons will continue to partner community organisations to offer pro-social support to abusers in the Drug Rehabilitation Centre (DRC) before they are emplaced on community rehabilitation programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Prisons will work with organisations, such as the Singapore Anti-Narcotics Association (SANA) and religious organisations under the Desistor Network, to invite desistors to share their experiences and motivate abusers through support groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As repeat abusers have more complex needs, Prisons has enhanced its psychology-based correctional programmes based on desistance and addictions studies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These programmes help abusers in the DRC better recognise their drug triggers and strengthen their resolve to resist drugs and pursue pro-social lifestyles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They also help abusers reflect on the harm that drugs have caused their loved ones and mend frayed relationships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After DRC, drug abusers are emplaced in the community under Prisons' supervision.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Tailored support from YRSG career coaches help them manage challenges, like stress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These help to reduce the risk of relapse and ease abusers back into the society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: After completing their community-based programmes, the now ex-abusers are placed under the supervision of CNB.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: CNB will monitor them for up to five years – through regular urine or hair tests to ensure they stay clean.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For ex-abusers with greater integration needs, case details will be shared between CNB and Prisons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This tight coordination amongst Home Team agencies ensures ex-abusers continue receiving the interventions they need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Previously, supervisees had to report to CNB for urine testing frequently, as often as twice a week.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will reduce disruption to supervisees' lives and the stigma associated with reporting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: CNB is piloting this and will study the results before full implementation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To fight the scourge of drugs, we must also intensify enforcement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will operationalise the amendments made last year to the Misuse of Drugs Act to enable CNB to enforce more quickly against NPS, which is a growing threat.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The HTX is developing novel NPS testing capabilities to enable this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will also continue to collaborate with other countries to curb drug supply into Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In 2023, CNB conducted 19 joint operations and investigations with foreign counterparts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One such operation led to the arrest of a Singaporean in Seoul involved in transnational drug trafficking on Telegram.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to partner the community and innovate in corrections, rehabilitation and reintegration to get even better re-offending outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I encourage Members of this House to show your support by wearing the green ribbon for a drug-free Singapore and the yellow ribbon for giving second chances to ex-offenders – like what I have on here as well as Minister Shanmugam, Minister Josephine Teo and Minister of State Sun Xueling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Members can collect these ribbons at the Parliament Library.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, on that note, thank you, Mr Chairman.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, we must press on in the war against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In this fight, fellow Singaporeans, residents and Government agencies are on the same battle front, defending ourselves against bad actors who are out to scam Singaporeans of hard-earned monies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Scams are a big problem around the world, not just in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Australia reported a loss of more than A$3.1 billion in 2022, an 80% increase from 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the United States, more than US$10 billion was lost to fraud in 2023, up by 72% from US$5.8 billion in 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The 2023 statistics on scams in Singapore show us where our weaknesses are and where further work needs to be done.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And 2023 was the first time in five years that we actually saw a slight decrease in scam losses from the year before.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In many of these cases, the victims initiated the transfer of monies to scammers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We know this because the top 10 scams in terms of number of victims included job scams, e-commerce scams and fake friend call scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Victims of these scams believed in the fake job or e-commerce offers promoted to them, or that calls made to them by scammers pretending to be their friends were real.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Such scams rely more on social engineering rather than technological sophistication.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In fact, one could say that these are old fashioned fraud conducted through online means.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Derrick Goh and Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi asked how we can reduce such scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As individuals, our optimism bias leads us to mistakenly believe that we will not be deceived.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We may also let our guard down, making us vulnerable to our inherent human desire to be loved, to make an extra buck, to seize an attractive looking offer and so on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That is why even younger Singaporeans, who are generally more digitally savvy, fall prey to scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Thus, even as we ramp up our digital and technical defences against scammers, we must not lose sight that public education remains key in our fight against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our best defence is an aware, watchful and discerning public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To help our citizens identify and protect themselves from scams that Mr Christopher de Souza spoke about, we have launched the Add, Check, Tell (ACT) campaign: (a) Add security features, such as ScamShield and multi-factor authentication for personal accounts; (b) Check for signs of scams; and (c) Tell the authorities and others about your scam encounters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi and Mr Keith Chua asked how we can better support vulnerable groups, such as the elderly, as part of scam prevention efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government works with partners to roll out targeted programmes for different segments of the population.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, to reach out to the elderly, the Police weaves anti-scam messages into "Getai" shows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SPF also works with Silver Generation Ambassadors to educate the elderly on scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To respond to Mr Gan Thiam Poh, we will further boost our public education efforts by consolidating anti-scam resources into a one-stop portal on scams this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The website will include information on what you should do if you think you have fallen prey to a scam, how you can protect yourself, as well as the latest scam trends.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It will also provide information on where victims of scams can seek support, which Assoc Prof Razwana Begum spoke about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, Police can activate volunteer Victim Care Officers (VCOs) to look into their needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The VCOs can then direct the victims to community and professional resources for psychological and financial support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government is also studying additional measures to better support unwitting members of the public, including those who refuse to believe that they are being scammed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They could be victims of love scams or investment scams where they have invested affection or significant amounts of monies, making it difficult for them to extract themselves out of the situation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum spoke about the importance of community partnerships in tackling scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To build a vigilant online community, we will expand existing community initiatives to include cybercrimes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes the Cyber Guardians on Watch and Crime Prevention Ambassador (Cyber) programmes which will be launched later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Mr Sitoh Yih Pin has pointed out, scammers are constantly evolving their modus operandi to get around our defences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have moved aggressively to put in technical defences to pre-empt this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As a result, we saw improvements in the phishing scams situation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The number of reported phishing cases in 2023 decreased by 16% from the year before, and the amounts lost decreased by 14%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In 2023, malware-enabled scams emerged as a scam of concern.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Government agencies acted swiftly with the banks to implement a series of measures to secure CPF and bank accounts, such as Singpass Face Verification for high-risk CPF transactions and anti-malware security features on banking apps.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, to bypass the blocking of overseas calls, more scammers are using Singapore SIM cards to make scam calls and send SMSes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also enhancing ScamShield to improve the accuracy of scam SMS detection and allow users to report scams more easily.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the fight against scams, partners are essential.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Mr Derrick Goh said, the co-location of staff from banks at the Anti-Scam Command has facilitated faster tracing of scam proceeds and recovery of victims' monies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This initiative was recently expanded to include the co-location of Carousell staff.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As a result, the turnaround time for taking down online monikers involved in scams and suspicious advertisements on Carousell has now been reduced from days to hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to engage key stakeholders to co-locate at the Anti-Scam Centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We implemented measures to block scam calls and SMSes, but scammers then pivoted to social media and messaging apps to reach out to victims.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked how the Government works with online platforms to better protect Singaporeans from scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MHA and SPF have been engaging online platforms, specifically those which account for a large number of scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some, like Shopee and Carousell, have been willing and are working closely with MHA and the Police, such as by strengthening their user verification processes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In December 2022, Shopee introduced the seller verification features where sellers were required to verify their identities against Government records.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Other platforms have been less willing to implement additional measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, Meta has consistently pushed back against MHA's recommendations for them to put in place safeguards to combat e-commerce scams on Facebook, such as verifying users against Government issued ID and offering a secured payment option for Marketplace users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is despite Facebook contributing close to 50% of e-commerce scam cases in 2023.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is the only platform amongst those rated in MHA's E-commerce Marketplace Transaction Safety Ratings that has not implemented or commenced implementing the recommended safety features.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As a result, Facebook Marketplace was ranked the lowest in the Transaction Safety Ratings for the second consecutive year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I urge Meta to step up to do right by your users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: OCHA will also allow us to issue Codes of Practice to put in place systems, processes and measures to disrupt scams affecting people in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked if we will do more to attract investments and incentivise financial institutions to further develop anti-scam capabilities in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to drive the industry's anti-scam efforts through the Association of Banks in Singapore's Standing Committee on Fraud to implement robust measures to safeguard customers and reinforce public confidence in the security of digital banking.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The transnational nature of scams necessitates international cooperation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Under Singapore's Presidency of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), we have made fostering global cooperation to strengthen asset recovery one of our priorities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, we have facilitated the agreement across FATF member countries to strengthen global standards on the recovery of criminal proceeds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These standards will require countries to enhance their laws on the freezing, seizing and confiscation of assets, and international cooperation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To further forge international partnerships to tackle scams, Singapore will participate in the inaugural Global Fraud Summit in March this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   In 2023, the total number of cases showed an upward trend.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Among all the scam cases, the three most common types of scams with the highest number of victims were: job scams, e-commerce scams and fake friend call scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is evident that perpetrators primarily manipulate victims through social means, rather than using complex technological means.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ninety-two percent of the losses in scam cases resulted from scammers using social engineering tactics and fraudulent schemes to deceive victims into transferring monies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In many of these scam cases, victims often transfer monies to the scammers themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: All of this indicates the importance of enhancing public awareness and maintaining vigilance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, adding the anti-scam application ScamShield and anti-virus applications, as well as looking out for signs of scams and double-checking the identity of recipients before making any transfers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will explore additional measures to protect the public, including those who refuse to believe that they are being scammed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have made significant progress in preventing and blocking scam calls and SMSes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are exploring how to better utilise technology to detect scams and make it easier for the public to identify and report scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to pool efforts from various parties to combat scam syndicates and recover scammed monies. : I will now briefly speak about the security industry, who is our key partner in keeping Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum asked about the skill development of security officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Under the refreshed security industry transformation (ITM) 2025, we will continue to drive the upskilling of security officers so that they are better equipped to operate new integrated solutions and models, such as integrated facilities management.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will do so in close consultation with industry stakeholders to ensure that the training provided is accessible and relevant to all officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On the TOPSIS framework – which Assoc Prof Raswana Begum spoke about – the SPF Centre for Protective Security offers training for organisations who are interested to implement the TOPSIS framework at their premises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Both Assoc Prof Razwana Begum and Ms Sylvia Lim asked questions related to the welfare of security officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MHA and tripartite partners are actively looking at these issues as one of the means to help with the recruitment and retention.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are, of course, also very interested in maintaining the welfare of our security officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Members will be aware, wages of security officers have been raised and will continue to increase at a sustainable and meaningful pace through the Progressive Wage Model (PWM).

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government – together with its tripartite partners – are monitoring the implementation of the new wage schedule and will review further the working hours and deployment patterns of security officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our recent initiatives have implications on resourcing and we will need to monitor the industry's response to these initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked if there has been any change in the demographic profile of security officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The demographic profile of security officers has remained stable, with the average age of security officers being about 52 years old.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With growing integration of technology and advanced systems, anecdotally, we do see growing interest from younger Singaporeans and that is very encouraging.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On Ms Sylvia Lim's question on the source countries being considered for the recruitment of APOs, the four countries cited by the Member are not the sole sources being considered.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: All APOs must pass a basic English proficiency test, but it is not the sole requirement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On Ms Sylvia Lim's questions on the limits of duties that can be outsourced from SPF to APOs, I would like to clarify that only Police officers, forensic specialists and medical practitioners can conduct forensic medical examinations, otherwise known as FME.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: APOs may be involved only to support the conduct of the FME.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I seek clarification from the hon Minister in relation to the recruitment of volunteers for the Home Team's mission.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I recall him mentioning that actually recruitment is on the up.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I had actually obtained the figures through Parliamentary Questions filed in November 2023.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: And in respect of recruitment figures for VSC – between 2018 and 2022 – I see a drop.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Every succeeding year from 2018, it was actually a downward trend as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I would suggest perhaps some effort be put in to increase the recruitment, particularly given that VSC is a venerated organisation that would celebrate its 80th anniversary in two years' time.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For COP volunteers, I understand from the answer provided to me in November 2023 – that the statistics were started to be recorded from 2019 onwards.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, the numbers again were 1,086 for 2019 and – save for a spike in 2021 – it went down to 953 in 2022.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Notwithstanding the figures, I think the hon Minister and I agreed on the point that these volunteers serve as a valuable multiplier effect.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Mr Chairman, I see that more as a comment.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the specific data, I do not have it with me.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the Member files a question, I will check it out.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have pointed out that MPs are automatically PSPs, for example.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As regard to whether we will announce each time, I do not want to tie a future Government's actions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We think it makes sense to announce it so that Singaporeans are aware and hopefully it also shapes some behaviour.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Second question is whether it is a requirement – if someone becomes a member of a foreign legislature, whether they must declare it themselves?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I indicated that there are two different points.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You declare if you are a member of a foreign legislature or foreign political organisation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In fact, the deadline for declaration is today.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But that does not automatically lead to the designation of a PSP.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For precise requirements, rather than trying to set it out here, the Act sets it out quite clearly.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Minister for responding to parts of what I had raised in terms of the Thailand example of decriminalising cannabis plant for the purposes of supporting medical use and research purposes.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: The Minister did respond and he also put in a caveat to say that there is going to be a Ministerial Statement later on in the year, specifically on drugs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, I was hoping to use this opportunity to express my hope that that Statement would cover the example of the Thailand situation of decriminalising; and then what looks to be a U-turn and all the potential harm that has happened in between – as an example of how we must be extremely cautious in decriminalising the consumption of drugs in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, I reiterate my position that both consumption being the demand and trafficking being the supply should be deterred.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Thailand is obviously a relevant example – but bearing in mind we also need to be careful about how we talk about other countries, particularly the nearer they are to us and they are ASEAN members.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think we need to exercise some considerable care.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There is another serious point which is that: Singapore is small; Thailand is big.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Just because we are able to do certain things here does not mean that others can do the same thing in their countries.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Likewise, we do not necessarily get brownie points for being able to do some things better.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have many limitations because of size, but we are also able to do certain things because of size.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, we need to apply that lens carefully to others.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But there is a point that two years ago, they changed in 2022 and then now, they see that — they are changing back.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There are some lessons for us from that, I think.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If I can quickly clarify a couple more points.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On Mr Pillai's point, actually, my people who are working rather hard have sent me the data.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The recruitment for, if I may say so, COPs for example.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But if you look at the volunteers – VSCs, for example – it was 838 last year.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The recruitment numbers for VSCs have gone up.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The overall numbers maybe a bit less – came down – but the actual recruitment numbers are now going up.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On Mr Gerald Giam's question, our position is that we will declare and we have put that in the law, but a future Government can always change the position.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, that is why I do not want to tie any future Government's position.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Just to be sure, my intention is not to put down any country, certainly not any ASEAN country or beyond ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: The point that I was trying to make is that the arguments by the lobbyists to each country are somewhat similar, wherever they lobby – that cannabis is not destructive, that cannabis is possibly good.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: If we are able to use a recent example where the reasons provided by the lobbyists have, perhaps, been proven as incorrect; then that provides even more firepower for us domestically to move the narrative against the legalisation of consumption.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: That was the point that I was trying to get across rather than to put any country down.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I fully accept that, and I think that is a fair point.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There were any number of interviews in 2022 where I was told that since Thailand is doing this, should Singapore not do this?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I said we do not necessarily do whatever other countries do.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We look at what is in Singapore's interest.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But the very same media outlets that asked me those questions have not come back to ask me: now that Thailand is reversing course, perhaps you are right and they were wrong.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They do not say that, because that does not fit in with their agenda, nor do the activists who were all trumpeting Thailand's actions, who have now gone quiet.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If not, Mr Murali, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I also would like to express my thanks to the hon Minister, hon Second Minister and two hon Ministers of State for their considered responses.
